title: "Function Calling"
description: "A mechanism for a model to request that an application execute a declared function with structured arguments."
term: "Function Calling"
letter: "F"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Function calling lets a language model indicate that an application
should run a particular function, such as looking up a record or
calculating a value. The application executes the function and can
return its result to the model.

## Technical explanation

An application declares available functions and input schemas. The model
generates a structured call request, but the application remains
responsible for validating arguments, authorizing the operation,
executing it, and handling errors. Tool or function-calling formats vary
between model providers.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Function calling connects model outputs to existing software and data
systems. It can make workflows more capable, but introduces risks from
invalid arguments, excessive permissions, side effects, and untrusted
input.

## How it works

The application sends the model a user request and function
specifications. The model may return a structured call. Application code
validates and executes that call, then optionally sends the result back
to the model to produce a final response.

## Practical example

A travel assistant can request an availability lookup using a declared
search function. The application validates dates and destination,
executes a read-only query, and returns matching options for the model
to summarize.

## Common misconceptions

- The model proposes a function call; application code decides whether
  and how to execute it.
- A JSON schema does not replace authorization or server-side validation.
- Function calling is not the same as the model directly executing
  arbitrary code.
